questions.question: What does a graph's horizontal axis usually show in a simple experiment?
choices: The investigator's conclusion
Only the graph's title
The independent variable
The dependent variable in every experiment

questions.question: What does a graph's vertical axis usually show in a simple experiment?
choices: Only the instrument name
The control group's label in every experiment
Only the date of publication
The dependent variable

questions.question: Which graph is generally best for comparing separate categories?
choices: Bar graph
Unlabeled line graph
Scatterplot with no category labels
Map without a scale

questions.question: Which graph is commonly useful for showing change over time?
choices: An unordered list of symbols
A line graph
A single unlabeled bar
A diagram without values

questions.question: What is the arithmetic mean of a data set?
choices: The sum of the values divided by the number of values
The difference between the greatest and smallest values
The most frequent value only
The middle value after sorting only

questions.question: What is the median?
choices: The total of all values
The most frequent value
The middle value or mean of the two middle values in ordered data
The largest value minus the smallest value

questions.question: What is an outlier?
choices: The average of all measurements
A value unusually far from the rest of the data
The label of a control group
A value that must always be deleted

questions.question: Why should graph axes include units?
choices: Units make every relationship causal
Units guarantee the absence of errors
Units determine which conclusion must be chosen
Units help readers interpret the values correctly

questions.question: What does a positive association in a scatterplot mean?
choices: Larger values of one variable tend to occur with larger values of the other
One variable definitely causes the other
All points must lie exactly on a straight line
The two variables always have identical units

questions.question: Why can a truncated vertical axis make differences look larger?
choices: It changes the original measurements
It makes the sample more representative
It displays only a narrow portion of the full numerical scale
It removes outliers from the data

questions.question: Why should error bars be defined in a graph's caption?
choices: They always show the same quantity in every study
They may represent different measures of spread or uncertainty
They identify which hypothesis is correct
They eliminate uncertainty from the results

questions.question: What is interpolation?
choices: Predicting far outside the measured range
Replacing observations with expected values
Selecting only values that support a hypothesis
Estimating a value between measured data points

questions.question: Why should extrapolation be used cautiously?
choices: No graph can show a relationship
A trend may not continue outside the measured range
Measured values must all be wrong
A larger prediction always has a smaller uncertainty

questions.question: Why can a biased sample lead to misleading conclusions?
choices: It may not represent the population being studied
Every sample must include the entire population
It always contains too many measurements
It prevents calculation of an average

questions.question: What should a student do before deleting an unusual measurement?
choices: Remove it whenever it differs from the mean
Change it to the expected value
Keep only the highest values
Investigate possible causes and document any justified exclusion

questions.question: A plant's heights are 4, 6, and 8 centimeters over three measurements. What is the mean height?
choices: 4 centimeters
8 centimeters
6 centimeters
18 centimeters

questions.question: The ordered values are 2, 3, 4, 5, and 26. What is the median?
At 10 seconds, a temperature is 20°C; at 20 seconds, it is 30°C. Assuming a linear change between these points, what is the estimated temperature at 15 seconds?
A survey about school lunches includes only members of one sports team. What is the main concern?
choices: Survey data cannot use percentages
Athletes cannot answer survey questions
The sample may not represent the whole school
The survey must have more than one dependent variable

questions.question: Two groups have different average results, but their measurements vary widely. What additional information helps evaluate the difference?
choices: Sample sizes and measures of variation or uncertainty
Only the largest value from each group
Only whether the averages are whole numbers
Only the experiment's title
